events.text: The war is over and the hall of {wo_foe} is ash and broken tiles. Walking the last courtyard, you hear a sound from a grain jar by the kitchen wall: a breath held too long, let go. Inside, folded small, is a child of {wo_house}, eyes wide, clutching a wooden sword. {wo_name} does not cry. {wo_He} has decided, it seems, to be brave at you.

choices.text: Kneel so your eyes are level

effects.log: You kneel in the ash. After a long time {wo_name} puts the wooden sword down and takes your sleeve. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

choices.text: Put the lid back and stand guard

effects.log: You stand by the jar until the victors have gone past, laughing, toward the gate. Then you lift the lid again. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

The medic finds nothing wrong but hunger and fright, and looks at you strangely. Whose child is this, the look says. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

events.text: The sect's line has won its war, and the summoned disciples are told to search the enemy's outer halls for documents. You find no documents. You find a child of {wo_house} under a pile of winter robes, sound asleep, as only a child who has been awake for three days can sleep. A name is stitched into the collar: {wo_name}.

choices.text: Wrap the child in the robes and carry {wo_him} out

effects.log: Nobody stops a disciple carrying a bundle of robes. Not yet. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)
{wo_name} wakes, sees the colours you fought under, and goes very still. You put your own coat over them. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

events.text: The battle you fought for one side of the sects' war is won by evening. Walking the field after, you find the baggage carts of {wo_foe} overturned, and between two of them a child of {wo_house}, keeping very quiet with both hands over {wo_his} own mouth. {wo_name}, says the tag tied to {wo_his} wrist, so that someone could find {wo_him}.

effects.log: You take the small hands away from the small face. "It is over," you say. {wo_name} does not believe you yet. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

choices.text: Read the rest of the tag

effects.log: On the back, in a parent's hurried hand: "If you are kind, keep this child. If you are not, be quick." You are going to be kind. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

events.text: The throne's war is won and the enemy's border fort is taken. In the commander's quarters, behind a screen painted with cranes, the soldiers have missed a child: {wo_name} of {wo_house}, a commander's child, sitting very straight with {wo_his} hands folded, as {wo_he} must have been taught to sit when important people come.

effects.log: You sit. {wo_name} studies you and says, very politely, "Are you going to kill me?" You say no. {wo_He} nods as if that settles it. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)
The soldiers go. You close the door. Nobody else needs to know about the cranes. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

events.text: A child of {wo_house} in the ruins, {wo_name}, looking up at you out of a grain jar. You have never seen this child in your life. And yet your hands know exactly how to lift a child out of a jar without frightening it, as if they have done it before, in some other life, for some other war.

choices.text: Lift {wo_him} out the way your hands remember

effects.log: Your soul has done this before. It does it again. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

choices.text: Stop, and wonder whose hands these are

effects.log: A memory that is not yours: a child grown tall, bowing to you at a gate. Then it is gone, and the child in the jar is waiting. (What becomes of {wo_name} is yours to decide this year: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

events.text: Granny Bok of the reed village has buried three husbands and two wars and does not ask questions. She looks at {wo_name}, looks at you, looks at the colours you are not wearing today, and says only: "The child will need shoes." The reed village is far from both banners. Nobody there has ever heard of {wo_foe}.

choices.text: Leave silver for the shoes and more

effects.log: You leave enough for shoes for ten years. Granny Bok counts it twice and puts it in the rice jar.
"Visit, then," says Granny Bok. "Children remember who comes back."

choices.text: Teach {wo_name} the reed path out, in case

effects.log: {wo_name} learns the path through the reeds in an afternoon. Better a child who can run.

events.text: On the road to the reed village, {wo_name} rides on your back and asks questions in a whisper. Where are we going. Will there be dogs. Is the war following us. By the third day {wo_he} asks no questions at all, and falls asleep with {wo_his} cheek against your shoulder.

effects.log: You walk the last day at a crawl. Nobody has ever slept on your back before.

choices.text: Answer every question, truthfully except one

effects.log: Yes, there are dogs. No, the war is not following. You do not answer the one about whose side you were on.

events.text: You bring {wo_name} home. The household stares. A child of {wo_house}, of {wo_foe}, at your table, eating rice as if rice might be taken away. Nobody says anything. You say: "This is {wo_name}. {wo_He} lives here now." And so {wo_he} does.

effects.log: A small room with a window. {wo_name} sleeps on the floor beside the bed the first month, and then in it.
The wooden sword hangs on the wall. Some nights you hear {wo_him} talking to it.

events.text: Your sect's disciples line the hall when you bring the child of {wo_foe} through the gate. Some of them fought that war beside you. Some of them lost brothers in it. You stop in the middle of the hall with {wo_name} holding your hand, and you let them look as long as they like.

effects.log: Nobody answers. Nobody needs to. Your word is the sect's word.
You say nothing. After a while the eldest disciple steps forward and bows to the child. Then another. Then all of them.

events.text: You hand {wo_name} over to your side. The hostage master writes the name in a ledger with a neat brush and takes the child by the shoulder. {wo_name} does not look back at you. That is the worst of it: {wo_he} does not look back at all, as if {wo_he} had expected nothing else.

effects.log: The hostage master says hostages are always fed well. A thin hostage is worth less.

choices.text: Walk away and do not look back either

effects.log: You do not look back. Your heart does, for years.

events.text: You waited too long. Your side's officers come for the child of {wo_foe} before you have decided anything, with a writ and a cart. "Prisoners of the war belong to the victors," the officer says, not unkindly. {wo_name} climbs into the cart without being told.

effects.log: {wo_name} looks at you as if you are speaking another language. Then the cart goes.
It is out of your hands now. You tell yourself that for a long time.

events.text: At the gate of what is left of {wo_foe}, an old guard sees your colours and reaches for a spear. Then {wo_name} shouts a name, an aunt's name, and the gate opens, and a woman comes running across the courtyard with her arms already out. Nobody thanks you. Nobody attacks you either. You walk back through the lines under your white banner.

choices.text: Bow to the gate before you go

effects.log: You bow. After a long moment, the old guard bows back. It is the first bow between your two sides in years.
{wo_name} waves back from the aunt's arms until the road bends.

events.text: Elder Cheon Mugak of your sect lost his only disciple in the war against {wo_foe}. He has found out about {wo_name}. He stands in your doorway with the sect's seal in his hand. "A child of that house, under our roof," he says. "Give the child to the sect's hostage hall, or answer for it before the elders."

effects.log: You stand before the elders and answer for it. They do not like your answer. You keep the child.
Elder Cheon takes {wo_name} by the wrist. He does not look triumphant. He looks tired. So do you.

ok.log: Elder Cheon listens to the end. "My disciple would have liked this child," he says at last, and leaves the seal on the table.

fail.log: He does not listen. "Then answer before the elders," he says, and you do.

events.text: Your elders know whose child {wo_name} is. They come to you as their head, carefully, all together, the way people carry a pot that is too hot. "The sect will say nothing," says the eldest. "But the sect is asking you to think about it."

effects.log: The elders bow and go. The child stays. The sect says nothing, as promised, for a while.
You send the child away, for the sect. It is the right thing for a head to do, you tell yourself.

events.text: An old man in faded robes asks for you at the gate. Gu Haemun, he says, the last elder of {wo_house}. He has walked every road between here and the river asking after a child of that house. "They say you found one," he says. "I would like to see {wo_name} once, before I die. Or take {wo_him} home, if {wo_he} will come."

effects.log: Gu Haemun weeps when he sees {wo_name}, and {wo_name} weeps when {wo_he} sees him, and you walk them both to the road.

choices.text: Let him see the child, and nothing more

effects.log: Gu Haemun sits with {wo_name} an hour, and asks {wo_him} nothing, and leaves. At the gate he says: "One day {wo_he} will ask whose side you fought on."
Gu Haemun looks at you for a long time. "Then I am sorry to have troubled you," he says, and goes. He does not believe you.

events.text: Gu Haemun, the last elder of {wo_house}, finds the reed village before he finds you. Granny Bok sends word: an old man sits by the river every day watching {wo_name} play, and says nothing, and goes away at sunset. She wants to know if she should chase him off with the broom.

choices.text: Tell her to let him watch

effects.log: The old man watches for a month. Then he leaves a carved wooden bird on the doorstep and does not come back.

choices.text: Go and meet him by the river

effects.log: He knows who you are. "Thank you for keeping {wo_him} alive," he says. "Now let {wo_him} come home." You let {wo_him} choose, and {wo_he} goes.

events.text: {wo_name} has started following you to the training yard at dawn and copying your forms from behind a pillar, with the wooden sword, very seriously. {wo_His} footwork is wrong in the way all children's footwork is wrong. Nobody has told {wo_him} that {wo_his} stance is the stance of {wo_foe}.

effects.log: You correct it gently, toward your own style. {wo_name} learns fast.

choices.text: Leave the stance as it is

effects.log: You leave it. The child's family left {wo_him} very little. {wo_He} can keep the stance.

events.text: There is a fever in the house, and {wo_name} has it. For three nights you sit by the bed with a cold cloth. On the third night {wo_he} wakes and asks for a parent by a name you have never heard. Then {wo_he} sees it is you, and says, "Oh," and goes back to sleep holding your hand.

effects.log: The fever breaks at dawn. You have not slept. You find you do not mind.
You remember the name. One day {wo_name} may want to know it was spoken.

events.text: At the New Year festival, a neighbour's child shouts at {wo_name}: "Your real family were the bad side!" {wo_name} comes home with a torn sleeve, bright-eyed and silent, and asks you only one thing: "Were they?"

effects.log: {wo_name} thinks about that for a whole day, and then mends {wo_his} own sleeve.

choices.text: "They were your family. That is enough."

effects.log: {wo_name} nods. You have not answered the real question, and you both know it.

choices.text: Go and speak to the neighbour

effects.log: The neighbour apologises, red to the ears. {wo_name} is not bothered again.

events.text: You visit the reed village. {wo_name} has grown a hand taller and can name every bird in the reeds. Granny Bok says {wo_he} asks after you every market day, and pretends not to.

choices.text: Bring a present from the city

effects.log: A painted kite. {wo_name} flies it until dark, and keeps the string wound on a stick under {wo_his} pillow.

choices.text: Help Granny Bok mend the roof

effects.log: You mend the roof. {wo_name} hands you nails and tells you everything that happened in the last year, all at once.

events.text: Granny Bok is getting old. She says so plainly over tea, with {wo_name} out of earshot. "Not this year. Maybe not next. But you should know who that child will have when I am gone." She looks at you over the cup.

effects.log: Granny Bok nods once. That was the only answer she was going to accept.

choices.text: Leave silver for the years ahead

effects.log: She puts it in the rice jar with the rest. "Silver is not a person," she says. "But it helps."

events.text: You tell {wo_name} the truth: the war, {wo_foe}, the grain jar, and whose side you fought on that day. {wo_name} listens without moving. When you finish, {wo_he} stands up, very carefully, as if something might spill, and walks out of the room.

effects.log: You wait. It is the longest night of your life. At dawn {wo_name} comes back and sits down across from you again, and says nothing, and stays.
{wo_name} walks to the river and throws stones into it until the stones run out. You stand where {wo_he} can see you. It is all you can do.

events.text: Years ago you told {wo_name} the truth yourself. Now {wo_he} is grown enough to understand it, and comes to you with the old wooden sword in both hands. "You fought them," {wo_he} says. "And you carried me out. I have decided which one of those I am going to remember."

effects.log: "Both," says {wo_name}. "But the second one more." {wo_He} hangs the wooden sword back on the wall.
{wo_name} is too old for it, and does it anyway.

events.text: A drunk veteran at the market recognises {wo_name}'s face from the war and says too much: whose side you were on, what you did that day. {wo_name} comes home and stands in the doorway a long time. "I heard," {wo_he} says. Then: "I don't care. You came back for me. Nobody else did."

effects.log: You tell {wo_him} all of it. {wo_name} listens to the end, and still stays.
It is the only thing you can say. {wo_name} understands.

events.text: {wo_name} has found out whose side you fought on, from a stranger, from a letter, it does not matter. You come home and the old wooden sword is snapped in two on the table, and {wo_name} is gone. There is no note. The broken sword is the note.

effects.log: You wrap the halves in silk. One day {wo_he} may come back for them, or for you.
You search the roads for a month and find nothing. A child you taught to disappear has learned it well.

events.text: {wo_name} has become a fighter in {wo_his} own right, and takes your side in every quarrel of the murim without being asked, so fiercely that you have to hold {wo_him} back. "Somebody has to," {wo_he} says, when you ask why.

effects.log: It takes a year. {wo_name} learns it better than you ever did.
The two of you are a sight on the road. People start to talk about you as a pair.

events.text: On the anniversary of the war, {wo_name} goes alone to the ruins of {wo_foe} to burn incense for the family {wo_he} does not remember. This year {wo_he} asks you to come too. You stand side by side in the ash where you found {wo_him}.

effects.log: You burn incense for the people you fought. {wo_name} watches you do it, and something settles between you for good.
You stand at the broken gate. When {wo_name} comes back, {wo_his} eyes are red and {wo_he} takes your arm.

events.text: Gu Haemun, the last elder of {wo_house}, dies at last, and leaves {wo_name} the one thing the war did not burn: the family's own martial art, written on silk and sewn into the lining of a winter coat. {wo_name} brings it to you unopened. "It should be read by both of us," {wo_he} says, "or by nobody."

effects.log: You read it together over a winter. It is a fine art, and it knew your own style once: your two families crossed swords for a hundred years. (A family's lost manual)
{wo_name} reads it alone, then teaches it to you, slowly, the way you once taught {wo_him} to stand. (A family's lost manual)

events.text: {wo_name} is at your gate, grown, with a real sword this time, and the stance of {wo_foe}, the stance you never corrected. "I have come to settle the war," {wo_he} says. "You know which war." (Face {wo_him}, talk, or lower your sword: The Enemy's Child, in the Jianghu.)

effects.log: You open the gate. Whatever comes, it will not come through a closed door.

choices.text: Bring out the two halves of the wooden sword

effects.log: You set them on the step between you. {wo_name}'s sword-point wavers, for a breath.

events.text: {wo_name} stays for dinner, in the end. Nobody mentions the sword leaning in the corner. Halfway through the meal {wo_he} reaches over and puts the best piece of fish in your bowl, the way you used to do for {wo_him}, and that is the whole of the peace treaty.

effects.log: It is very good fish.

choices.text: Put a piece in {wo_his} bowl too

effects.log: You go back and forth until the fish is gone, and you are both laughing.

events.text: {wo_name} leaves without finishing it. Not because {wo_he} cannot, you think, but because {wo_he} has found out that {wo_he} does not want to. The road takes {wo_him}. You never quite stop looking for {wo_his} face in crowds.

choices.text: Light a lamp in the window

effects.log: You light it every night for a year. Then every New Year. Then you stop counting.
You let {wo_him} go. It is the second time you have had to, and it is no easier.

events.text: Six years after you walked {wo_name} home through the lines, a letter comes from {wo_foe}, in a young hand. {wo_name} is well, studies hard, and has been told by an aunt who carried {wo_him} home. The last line says: "When the two sides are at peace, I will come and thank you myself."

effects.log: You write back. You keep writing, every spring, across the old lines.
You keep the letter in your sleeve until the paper goes soft.

events.text: At a crossroads shrine you have never visited, there is an old tablet with a name carved on it that is not your name in this life, and under it: "Who carried a child out of the ashes of a war." Somebody still leaves fresh incense here.

effects.log: Your hands shake a little, and you do not know why.

choices.text: Ask the shrine keeper who leaves it

effects.log: "A family that was saved once," says the keeper. "They have forgotten why. They still come."

events.text: In the street a stranger's child drops a toy and looks up at you, and you are suddenly certain, without any reason, that you once handed a child like that to people who would not be kind. Your chest aches for a whole day.

choices.text: Pick up the toy and give it back

effects.log: The child takes it and runs off. Something in you that was clenched lets go, a little.
You walk on. The ache comes with you.

events.text: A young fighter on the road stops you with a sword half drawn, stares at your face, and slowly puts it away. "Sorry," the fighter says. "For a moment you looked like someone my teacher's teacher had a war with, and made peace with, over a plate of fish." You laugh, and do not know why your eyes sting.

choices.text: Offer to buy the fighter a meal

effects.log: You eat together. Neither of you orders the fish. Both of you think about it.
"With dinner," says the fighter. "It always ends with dinner."

events.text: Crossing an old battle line that is only a farm road now, you have the sudden certainty that you once walked a frightened child across it under a white banner, and handed the child to people who wept. The farmers stare at you standing still in the middle of the road.

choices.text: Bow to the far side of the road

effects.log: You bow. A farmer on the far side, puzzled, bows back.
You walk on. Something in your soul is proud of you, and will not say why.

events.text: In a reed village you have never visited, an old woman at a doorway looks at you and says, "The child is grown. Did you come back for the shoes?" Then she shakes her head and goes inside, embarrassed. You stand in the reeds for a long time.

choices.text: Leave a little silver on the step

effects.log: You leave it, for shoes, for anyone.
The wind in the reeds sounds like a child naming every bird.
